newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet adopts plan for energy sector sale.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet adopts plan for energy sector sale.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday adopted a plan to relax the state's grip over the energy sector, paving the way for the industry's privatisation within the next nine years, the industry minister said.

"The process of the sector's privatisation should be completed by the year 2005," Klemens Scierski told a news briefing after the government approved a document called "The electricity sector's demonopolisation and privatisation."
"By the year 2000 all smaller power and heating plants should be privatised as well as a substantial part of larger power stations," he added.
The plan envisages selling majority stakes in power stations to domestic or foreign investors or floating their shares on the bourse.
The implementation of the scheme depends on whether parliament approves a new energy law designed to adopt communist-era regulations to market conditions and Western standards.
The government hopes the bill would be passed next month.
The law would allow electricity producers to compete with one another and would pave the way for gradual liberalisation of energy prices.
Under the law, customers would be able to shop around for best energy prices. Companies now buy energy from the nearest supplier at government controlled prices.
Deputy Industry Minister Herbert Gabrys, also present, said Polish energy prices should reach world levels between 2004 and 2005.
Under the programme, the government would keep control over the national power grid (PSE), which by law will have to guarantee all electricity producers equal access to its network.
Several pilot privatisation projects are already underway in the energy sector with the biggest one, the sale of the Patnow-Adamow-Konin (PAK) power plants complex, due to be completed next year.
Poland's energy sector, employing 120,000 people, generates about five percent of Poland's gross domestic product forecasted at 427 billion zlotys next year.
The industry's value is estimated at 90 billion zlotys, Scierski said. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
